root_cause.text: The function `rtnl_fill_vfinfo() in net/core/rtnetlink.c` fails to zero-initialize the on-stack `struct ifla_vf_broadcast` before performing a partial `memcpy` (based on `dev->addr_len`, typically 6 bytes), leaving 26 uninitialized bytes that are then copied to userspace via `nla_put`, causing a stack information leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `memset(&vf_broadcast, 0, sizeof(vf_broadcast));` before `memcpy(vf_broadcast.broadcast, dev->broadcast, dev->addr_len);`, and the commit message explicitly states that the struct has a 32-byte field but only 6 bytes are written on Ethernet devices, leaving the remaining bytes uninitialized and leaked to userspace.

vuln_statements.explanation: This partial memcpy copies only dev->addr_len bytes (typically 6) into the on-stack struct ifla_vf_broadcast, which is not zero-initialized. The remaining 26 bytes of the broadcast field (and any padding) are uninitialized and will be leaked to userspace via nla_put.

While this memcpy copies a full-size MAC address and does not directly cause a leak, it is part of the same non-initialized local variable pattern where on-stack structs (like vf_mac) may also have uninitialized padding bytes. It is included as a related statement in the vulnerable code path.

This assignment is part of the same function block that copies virtual function information. While not directly leaking data, it demonstrates the pattern of filling struct fields without zeroing the entire struct, contributing to the overall lack of initialization.

This assignment sets the vlan field of a local struct vf_vlan that is not zero-initialized. Although the vlan and qos fields are both set, any padding bytes in the struct could remain uninitialized, posing a similar leak risk, though the primary leak is from vf_broadcast.

This assignment completes the vlan struct fill, but like its companion, it does not address struct padding. It is included as part of the broader non-zero-initialization context in the function that leads to a stack information leak.
